name: Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Palpa
description: Etched into the dry coastal plain of southern Peru, about 400 km south of Lima, these enormous drawings were made by clearing dark surface pebbles to reveal paler ground beneath. Between 500 BC and AD 500, the Nasca people created long straight lines, geometric shapes and more than 70 figures, including a hummingbird, monkey and condor. Many are best seen from the air, and their purpose, probably ritual, remains a mystery.
